Moving towards a more aggressive release cycle
Daily ISO builds are now a reliable installer, so new installs start close to current.
We are moving to libera.chat network
After the events on Freenode, #lunar moves to the Libera.Chat IRC network.
We are still very much alive
Yes, the project is alive: packages are updated almost daily, and daily ISOs fill in until the next release.
Lunar 1.7.0 "Sinus Successus" is released, with systemd, kernel 3.16 and an overhauled installer.
1.7.0-rc2 "Sinus Successus" switches to systemd and adds btrfs and initrd support.
Lunar's services have almost finished moving to their new hosts.
Services from lunar-linux.org may be disrupted
The project's hosting is ending, so services may be interrupted during the move.
The next installer ISO is in development, with a new build system, systemd and dracut.
One developer's git workflow for moonbase, with a branch for upstream work and one for local patches.
A fresh 32-bit chroot image for running 32-bit programs on a 64-bit installation.
Future use of MAINTAINER= in DETAILS
The MAINTAINER field in DETAILS starts to matter: ask a module's maintainer before changing it.
Users of theedge can now choose between a stable and an unstable moonbase branch.
The documentation wiki is updated to the latest MediaWiki, ahead of a new theme.
The module website gets the main site's template, cleaner markup and friendlier URLs.
Weighing the options for networking: improve our own scripts, or switch to wicd, NetworkManager or connman.
Add -rc to a line in the lunar update list to reconfigure that module's optional dependencies.
The website moves from Joomla to WordPress and starts collecting posts from developers' blogs.
A proposal for a SUPERSEEDED field in DETAILS, so updates can follow renamed modules.
A walkthrough of replacing the init system with systemd, and the network scripts with connman.
Updating old lunar installations: Getting rid of hal
How to remove the deprecated hal from an older installation and rebuild what depended on it.
An experiment that syncs moonbase into an SQLite database to speed up lunar's tools.
Lunar 1.6.5 "Mare Ingenii" is released, now as a hybrid ISO that installs from a USB stick.
1.6.5-rc1 "Mare Ingenii" brings kernel 2.6.34, ext4 support and ssh on the live CD.
Lunar 1.6.4 "Lacus Autumni" is released, almost two years after the previous stable ISO.
1.6.4-beta1 "Lacus Autumni" ships kernel 2.6.27, working software RAID and USB installs.
1.6.4-alpha3 "Lacus Autumni" is out for testing, with RAID, language menu and Grub fixes.
The website gets translation icons, and a call for volunteer translators.
The website moves to Joomla! 1.5 and loses polls and comments along the way.
The update steps needed after installing from the outdated 1.6.2 (or older) ISO.
The main server goes down for maintenance, and comes back up.
A new glibc brings UTF-8 locales and ends support for the Linux 2.4 kernel.
XOrg in moonbase is updated to X11R7.3, with two caveats for mouse and NVIDIA users.
The 1.6.2 beta installs a basic Xfce desktop with XOrg 7.2, Firefox and other everyday applications.
A new lunar-init module takes over the core init scripts, and the switch needs a few manual steps.
Lunar 1.6.1 installer iso "Moose Drool" released for i686 and x86_64
Lunar 1.6.1 "Moose Drool" is released, including the first stable x86_64 ISO.
C++ support added to distcc and ccache
distcc and ccache can now cache and distribute C++ builds too.
Update the core tools before coreutils, so chown and chmod survive the upgrade.
New Madwifi-svn module / CVS module to be phased out
A madwifi-svn module replaces madwifi-cvs, and a stable madwifi module is added.
A new drm-git module replaces libdrm-cvs for 3D acceleration under XOrg 7.
XOrg in moonbase is updated to X11R7.1.
udev 101 arrives in moonbase with a new rules patchset, and may ask for a few missing groups.
The modular XOrg 7.0 tree lands in moonbase's zbeta section, with a guide for upgrading.
The 1.6.0 ISO leaves the kernel sources unconfigured; one command fixes it.
Lunar 1.6.0 "Indium Antimonide" is released, the first stable ISO based on the 2.6 kernel.
Lunar Linux gets its own group on Last.fm.
Release candidate 3 of 1.6.0 adds a software RAID tool to the installer and SELinux kernels.
Release candidate 2 of 1.6.0 adds dmidecode, ethtool, RAID drivers and tuned server kernels.
Release candidate 1 of 1.6.0 brings an NPTL-enabled glibc and rewritten SATA detection.
The first alpha of the 1.6.0 installer, the first ISO built on a 2.6 kernel with udev, hotplug and sysfs.
Release candidate 1 of the 1.5.2 installer ISO is ready for testing.
Changes to thunderbird and removal of linux-2.6-inotify
Enigmail support leaves the thunderbird module, and the linux-2.6-inotify kernel is removed now its patches are upstream.
gcc 3.4.4 and glibc 2.3.5 now in moonbase
gcc and glibc are updated in moonbase, with a list of modules worth recompiling afterwards.
Release candidate 1 of the 1.5.1 "Gallium Arsenide" installer ISO, for i686 and i386.
Lunar 1.5.1 "Gallium Arsenide" is released, the first time two ISOs (i686 and i386) ship together.
The new website goes live with a Mantis bug tracker, a MediaWiki wiki and phpBB2 forums.
The first post on the new website, which admits it has no actual news in it.
